“Would you be surprised?” Using the Surprise Question to Explore Medication Discontinuation

1 Study Overview

1.1 Background

The surprise question was developed over a decade ago and has been used in multiple settings to predict one year survival of different patient populations (e.g., to identify older hospitalized patients who may benefit from palliative or hospice care, to identify patients in the ED with a high risk of in-hospital mortality, predicting mortality for dialysis patients). The surprise question simply asks healthcare providers “would you be surprised if the patient died in the next 12 months?” No additional clinical data is needed. The predictive value of the surprise question has ranged from poor to reasonably accurate.

This quality improvement project would be to pilot the “surprise question” in select specialty clinics to assess its prognostic value in predicting patient outcomes. In Asthma and Allergy (ASAP) and Dermatology, pharmacists answered the question “Would you be surprised if this patient had a PDC of less than 90 or dose interruptions totaling 28 days or more over the next 6 months?”. In Oncology and Neurology, pharmacists answered the question “Would you be surprised if this patient discontinued this medication in the next 90 days?”
